                                                                    Abstract                                   To move beyond purely reactive policies, recent work
                                                                                                            has begun to incorporate predictive structure into visuomo-
                                        Vision–Language–Action (VLA) models achieve strong gen-             tor models [17, 23, 30]. Some approaches learn latent dy-
                                        eralization in robotic manipulation but remain largely re-          namics or temporal abstractions to better capture how states
                                        active and 2D-centric, making them unreliable in tasks              evolve over time [7, 8, 24, 50], while others predict fu-
                                        that require precise 3D reasoning. We propose GeoPre-               ture observations such as RGB frames, depths, or point-
                                        dict, a geometry-aware VLA framework that augments a                based representations [6, 11, 12, 17, 36, 49]. Although
                                        continuous-action policy with predictive kinematic and ge-          these methods provide useful temporal signals, they often
                                        ometric priors. GeoPredict introduces a trajectory-level            remain view-independent and do not strictly enforce multi-
                                        module that encodes motion history and predicts multi-step          view or 3D geometric consistency, making it hard to reason
                                        3D keypoint trajectories of robot arms, and a predictive 3D         about object poses, clearances, and end-effector motion in
                                        Gaussian geometry module that forecasts workspace ge-               workspace coordinates. Moreover, tightly coupling high-
                                        ometry with track-guided refinement along future keypoint           capacity predictive modules with large VLA backbones can
                                        trajectories. These predictive modules serve exclusively as         introduce non-negligible computational overhead if com-
                                        training-time supervision through depth-based rendering,            plex 3D prediction is required during inference time.
                                        while inference requires only lightweight additional query             For robotic manipulation, we argue that two predic-

                                        RoboCasa Human-50, LIBERO, and real-world manipula-                 should exploit predictive kinematic priors that summarize
                                        tion tasks show that GeoPredict consistently outperforms            how the robot is likely to move over the next few steps,

Figure 1. Overview of GeoPredict. Given an instruction, multi-view images and motion history encoded by the Track Encoder, a central
LLM Transformer learns two main tasks. First, it predicts multi-timestep 3D keypoint trajectories using learnable Future Track Query.
Second, it forecasts future workspace geometry as a predictive 3D Gaussian by processing a 3D Spatial Query through a Voxel Decoder.
A track-guided refinement mechanism leverages the predicted future tracks to allocate geometric capacity to task-relevant interaction
regions. Our policy then generates the final action via an Action Expert. Crucially, these predictive modules serve exclusively as training-
time supervision and are not invoked during inference, thus preserving efficiency.

by the predictive 3D Gaussian geometry and its refinement                               the action expert then generates At by integrating a learned
mechanism (Sec. 3.3). Finally, we present the attention de-                             vector field from noise in a small, fixed number of steps.
sign, training objective and inference process (Sec. 3.4).

Block-wise Causal Attention Mechanism. We adopt a                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            ules (e.g., the voxel decoder and depth-rendering mod-
block-wise causal attention structure adapted from π0 as                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     ule) are not executed during inference. 4.1. Experimental Setup
Simulation Benchmarks. We evaluate our method on two
widely recognized robotic manipulation benchmarks.
• RoboCasa [34]: This benchmark features 24 complex
   long-horizon everyday tasks in kitchen environments.
   We adopt the challenging Human-50 few-shot setting,
   where policies are trained using only 50 human demon-
   strations per task. To rigorously assess generalization
   capabilities, we follow the standard protocol by evaluat-
   ing our model over 50 trials per task across five distinct
   scenes. This evaluation is conducted exclusively on un-
   seen object instances, and includes scenes with unseen
   styles that were never encountered during training.
• LIBERO [26]: This benchmark is designed to evalu-                    Spatial Generalization:       Geometry Generalization:       Visual Robustness:
   ate knowledge transfer and policy generalization across             Place the green cube into a   Place the green cube with      Place the yellow cube into
                                                                       plate located at unseen       varying geometric sizes into   the plate under unseen
   four distinct task suites: LIBERO-Spatial, LIBERO-                  spatial positions.            the plate.                     backgrounds.

   Object, LIBERO-Goal, and LIBERO-Long. We follow
